analysis.title: Liquid Insight - USD: Surfing the blue wave
key_insights: Two weeks after the US midterms (decisive Democratic victory), Brent has fallen about 11% on hopes of a faster US-Iran resolution and US tech has underperformed, yet US rates and the USD have risen.
BofA sees post-midterm effects as noise and stays bullish USD into H1 2027. A USD selloff is treated as an opportunity to fade, consistent with its 29 Sept note.

The USD's beta to Brent has been small and drifting lower. Over five years the USD's co-movement with oil has been almost entirely a function of how rate differentials react, so oil falling on war resolution is not a clear bearish USD signal.

BofA's base case is Brent averaging about $74/bbl in Q4 2027, roughly another 20% lower. A prolonged status quo of limited kinetic activity without a peace deal should keep global oil supply curtailed.

The tech selloff accelerated after the midterms on narratives about regulating the data center buildout. It has not pulled the USD lower because of the USD's negative correlation to risk appetite and higher yields (dollar smile).
BofA thinks the market may be over-indexing on the AI-regulation theme. It expects AI investment to add to 2027 growth, and clearer regulation could spark a recovery in chip stocks.
Inflows into the US in October remained robust even as a Democratic sweep became the market base case, though the trend has cooled.
In the FX and Rates Sentiment survey, roughly half of clients saw an AI wobble as USD-negative and half as neutral or supportive. About one quarter see it as the predominant driver of a USD selloff.
Hot October labor and inflation data make the Fed look behind the curve. Unemployment is 4.1% and core PCE is 3.1%. US economic surprise indices are at historically high levels.

Markets price small odds of a 50bp Fed hike in December. BofA economists are well above consensus, calling for three consecutive Fed hikes starting in December. The post-election Fed repricing is the biggest among G10.

Since 2020, in each of the 5 times the relative US economic surprise measure peaked above 1-sigma, DXY rallied an average of about 2% over the next 60 trading days. History suggests scope for a USD rally at least into Q1 even if data surprises have peaked.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD, fade any USD selloff into H1 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong US growth backdrop, hawkish Fed repricing and rate differentials support the dollar, and election-related fallout is noise.
trade_ideas.risk: A faltering AI rally weighing on US asset inflows, or US data deteriorating and forcing a more dovish Fed.

AI rally faltering further, weighing on US asset inflows and the USD.

tension_points.bull_case: Hot US data, hawkish Fed repricing and rate differentials support the USD. BofA expects three Fed hikes starting in December and USD gains into H1 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Conventional wisdom expects USD downside from lower oil, a tech selloff and growth downgrades. Survey respondents see softer US data and a faltering AI rally as the most likely catalysts for USD weakness.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US data deteriorating and forcing a more dovish Fed, or the AI rally faltering further and weighing on US asset inflows.
